book_title: How a Woman Becomes a Lake
email_body:
Dear Marjorie,

In How a Woman Becomes a Lake, it is Vera's absence, rather than her presence, that sets everything moving in Whale Bay, and I was struck by how a single disappearance ripples through so many lives. Coming after Y and your O. Henry Award story "Counterblast", it feels like a book built around what goes unseen.

I would love to ask how you decided whose eyes we follow through those reverberations.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is developed through a few written questions you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger

subject_line: The sleeping town of Santa Lora
email_body:
Dear Karen,

The Dreamers begins so quietly: a first-year student comes back to her dorm room, falls asleep, and simply doesn't wake up. From there the sickness spreads through Santa Lora, and the fictional Southern California town becomes a place where people sleep for days, weeks or months.

I would love to ask what draws you to the possibility of the impossible, and how you keep such a premise grounded in ordinary lives.
